title: Detecting Regulatory States in Natural Language: A Validation Study of the Four Nervous System States Gradient
summary: Initial computational study of regulatory-state markers in natural language, pre-registered as the Four-Mode Gradient. Using analysis of 10,000+ Reddit AITA posts, four regulatory-state patterns — Connection, Protection, Strategic Management, and Domination — were explored using markers drawn from polyvagal theory, attachment research, Gottman's contempt markers, and Bandura's moral disengagement theory. The study is grounded in a two-system architecture: an Emotional Somatic System (ESS) that detects and responds before conscious awareness, and a Cognitive-Logical System (CLS) that builds from whatever data reaches it.
keyFinding: Interoceptive Self-Awareness (SEA) — the bridge between the ESS and CLS, operationalized through complexity markers (ability to hold multiple perspectives) — may help distinguish de-escalation toward Connection from escalation toward Strategic Management/Domination when challenged. In this sample, de-escalators showed 78% higher complexity marker rates than escalators.
author: Anna Paretas-Artacho
versionHistory: Version 1.0 (January 2026): Initial preprint published as 'Four-Mode Gradient.' Version 2.0 (April 2026): Framework renamed to Four Nervous System States Gradient; ESS/CLS architecture added; clustering result reinterpreted as a structural question for the framework; self-awareness gate reframed through Interoceptive Self-Awareness (SEA). Methods and results unchanged.

content.title: Abstract
content.content:
This study presents an initial computational test of the Four Nervous System States Gradient (pre-registered as the 'Four-Mode Gradient'), a theoretical framework proposing that human regulatory states can be classified into four states — Connection, Protection, Strategic Management, and Domination — based on perceived safety or threat. The framework is grounded in a two-system architecture: an Emotional Somatic System (ESS) that detects, evaluates, and generates physiological responses before conscious awareness, and a Cognitive-Logical System (CLS) that builds from whatever data reaches it. Connection and Protection are ESS-led states; Strategic Management and Domination are states in which the CLS is increasingly recruited into threat organisation — a qualitative shift, not merely an intensification.

Using natural language analysis of 10,000+ Reddit AITA posts, we tested whether these four states could be detected using markers drawn from psychological constructs in polyvagal theory, attachment research, contempt markers (Gottman), and moral disengagement theory (Bandura). Regulatory-state marker patterns were detected in the sample. State classifications correlated meaningfully with external community judgments. Clustering analysis produced three distinct state clusters (Connection, Control, Domination), with Protection functioning as a transitional state — a finding that Version 2.0 treats as a structural question for further testing rather than as proof of the architecture.

Analysis of 1,294 posts where authors responded to negative feedback found that Interoceptive Self-Awareness (SEA) — operationalized through complexity markers (ability to hold multiple perspectives) — differentiated de-escalators (22.2%) from escalators (33.8%) in this sample, with de-escalators showing 78% higher complexity marker rates.

content.title: Key Findings
content.content:
1. Regulatory-state marker patterns were detected in natural language across 10,000+ posts. Connection dominated as the most frequent state (51.4% as dominant), followed by Strategic Management (29.7%), Protection (14.8%), and Domination (4.1%).

2. State classifications correlated meaningfully with community verdicts (N=11,670). YTA posters used more Connection/Protection language (self-favorable framing), while NTA posters described more Strategic Management/Domination — reporting what was done to them.

3. Three states clustered clearly in this analysis (Connection, Strategic Management, Domination). Protection did not form a separate cluster — it co-occurred with other states, functioning as a transitional state. Version 2.0 treats this as a structural question: ESS-led states (Connection, Protection) may be organised by the same system, while CLS-recruited states (Strategic Management, Domination) may share the defining quality of cognitive recruitment into threat organisation.

4. Of 1,294 posts with edit sections: 33.8% escalated toward Strategic Management/Domination, 22.2% de-escalated toward Connection, and 44.0% maintained the same state.

5. Complexity markers — operationalizing Interoceptive Self-Awareness (SEA), the bridge between the ESS and CLS — were 78% higher in de-escalators than escalators in this sample. Surface-level ownership ('I was wrong') without genuine complexity may be performative: the CLS producing accurate-sounding self-reflection without the internal state that would make it genuine.

content.title: Methodology
content.content:
Pre-registered observational study using natural language analysis (OSF: osf.io/f4x6y). Rather than imposing the four-state structure on data, each state was operationalized using established psychological constructs and tested for organic emergence.

Data source: Kaggle AITA Dataset (nird96) — Reddit 'Am I The Asshole' community. Sample sizes: 10,000+ posts for state detection, 11,670 posts for verdict analysis, 1,294 posts for escalation analysis.

Detection schema: Connection (LIWC affiliation, polyvagal safety cues, attachment linguistics), Protection (threat-response markers, anxiety markers, withdrawal patterns), Strategic Management (power discourse analysis, LIWC certainty, demand patterns), Domination (Gottman contempt markers, Bandura moral disengagement).

Self-awareness markers: Ownership (self-responsibility), Complexity (multiple perspective-taking), Deflection (other-blame), Attack (escalation).

Analysis: State detection via marker scoring, K-means clustering (k=2 through k=6), chi-square analysis of state distribution by community verdict, escalation trajectory classification, and self-awareness marker comparison between escalators and de-escalators.

content.title: Theoretical Contributions (Version 2.0)
content.content:
Version 2.0 documents the generative relationship between empirical observation and architectural development. Three findings drove theoretical precision:

1. The Protection clustering result raised a question the original framework could not answer: why does Protection co-occur with other states rather than standing alone? Answering this required articulating the ESS/CLS qualitative distinction — the difference between body-led and cognition-recruited states. The clustering data forced the precision.

2. The self-awareness gate finding raised a different question: what exactly is 'complexity' doing mechanically? The observation that perspective-taking predicted de-escalation while ownership alone did not required identifying Interoceptive Self-Awareness (SEA) as a distinct biological capacity — the channel through which the CLS receives the ESS's signals.

3. The ownership-performativity observation pushed further: how can a person produce accurate-sounding self-reflection without the internal state? This required mapping coherence without the body as a distinct CLS configuration — not dishonesty, but a system building narratives from incomplete data without knowing the data is incomplete.

The data came first. The precision followed.

content.title: Implications
content.content:
The central contribution shifts focus from state detection to trajectory: the question is not only 'what state are you in?' but 'is the interoceptive channel open?' — because an open channel may be part of what makes return to Connection possible regardless of current state.

Potential applications and research questions include conflict de-escalation through early identification of escalation patterns via complexity marker analysis, relationship-safety research around whether a person can receive feedback, therapeutic research targeting Interoceptive Self-Awareness (SEA) and perspective-taking capacity, online moderation research around high-escalation linguistic patterns, and education developing interoceptive self-awareness as a learnable, teachable capacity.

content.title: Limitations
content.content: Single data source — results require replication across different platforms and contexts. Self-report bias — AITA posts represent the author's framing; actual behavior may differ. English language only — marker dictionaries validated for English; cross-cultural validity untested. Cross-sectional design — cannot establish causality; longitudinal studies needed. Marker operationalization — complexity markers capture a behavioral expression of SEA, not SEA directly; development of more specific interoceptive-channel markers is a priority for future work.
